NONE: › specialized biology a relationship between two types of animal or plant in which each provides for the other the conditions necessary for its continued existence
（動物或植物間的）共生
› a relationship between people or organizations that depend on each other equally
（人或機構間的）相互依賴的關係，互依關係
B2 a sign, shape, or object that is used to represent something else
標誌，象徵
› something that is used to represent a quality or idea
（某種特性或思想的）代表，象徵
› a number, letter, or sign used in mathematics, music, science, etc.
符號，代號，記號
› An object can be described as a symbol of something else if it seems to represent it because it is connected with it in a lot of people's minds
象徵

example: A heart shape is the symbol of love.
心形是愛的象徵。
The wheel in the Indian flag is a symbol of peace.
印度國旗上的輪子象徵和平。
Compare
emblem
Water, a symbol of life, recurs as an image throughout her poems.
水作為生命的一種象徵，在她的詩歌中反覆出現。
The symbol for oxygen is O.
氧的化學元素符號是O。
The private jet is a symbol of wealth.
私人噴射機是財富的象徵。

NONE: C2 representing something else
代表的，象徵的
› used to refer to an action that expresses or seems to express an intention or feeling, but has little practical influence on a situation
（行為舉動）象徵性的，沒有甚麼實際影響的

example: The skull at the bottom of the picture is symbolic of death.
圖片底部的骷髏象徵死亡。
Five hundred troops were sent in, more as a symbolic gesture than as a real threat.
派來500人的部隊，只是一個象徵性的舉動，並不構成實質性的威脅。

NONE: › the use of symbols in art, literature, films, etc. to represent ideas
象徵手法

› specialized art, literature a type of art and literature developed in the late 19th century that tries to express ideas or states of mind rather than represent the real world, using the power of words and images
（文學和藝術中的）象徵主義

example: Religious symbolism is very characteristic of the paintings of this period.
宗教象徵手法是這個時期繪畫的重要特徵。
Compare
naturalism

NONE: › a writer or an artist connected with symbolism
象徵主義者，象徵派
› to represent something
象徵，代表

example: The lighting of the Olympic torch symbolizes peace and friendship among the nations of the world.
奧林匹克聖火的點燃象徵著世界各國人民的和平與友誼。

NONE: › the quality of having parts that match each other, especially in a way that is attractive, or similarity of shape or contents
對稱（性）；勻稱

› specialized mathematics in mathematics, the quality of having two parts that match exactly, either when one half is like an image of the other half in a mirror, or when one part can take the place of another if it is turned 90° or 180°
（數學中的）對稱（性）

example: The design of the house had a pleasing symmetry, its oblong shape being picked up in its elongated windows.
房子的設計透出一種賞心悅目的對稱美，狹長的窗戶使長方形的結構顯得更加和諧。
Compare
asymmetry (asymmetric)

NONE: B2 used to describe someone who shows, especially by what they say, that they understand and care about someone else's suffering
有同情心的，同情的
› If a character in a book or film is sympathetic, they are described or shown in such a way that you are able to understand the character's feelings, with the result that you like them.
（書或電影中的人物）能引起共鳴的，讓人同情的，讓人有同感的
C2 agreeing with or supporting
支持的，贊同的

example: He suffers from back trouble too, so he was very sympathetic about my problem.
他自己也受背痛的困擾，所以對我的煩惱深表同情。
She just needed someone who would lend a sympathetic ear to her (= listen to her in a kind and understanding way) once in a while.
她只是需要一個人能不時以一種理解的態度聽她傾訴。
Opposite
unsympathetic
She comes across as a more sympathetic character in the movie.
她在影片中扮演的角色很能引起觀眾的共鳴。
The party is considered to be sympathetic to/towards welfare reform.
這個政黨被認為對福利改革抱贊同態度。
Did he give your proposal/complaints a sympathetic hearing?
他是以贊同的態度傾聽你的建議／投訴嗎？

I: C2 to understand and care about someone's problems
› to support and agree with someone or something

example: I know what it's like to have migraines, so I really sympathize (with you).
我知道偏頭痛有多難受，所以我真的很同情你。
I sympathize with the general aims of the organization, but on this particular issue I disagree.
我支持這個機構的總目標，但在這個具體議題上，恐怕我不能苟同。

NONE: › a person who supports a political organization or believes in a set of ideas
支持者；信奉者

example: He had been a known IRA sympathizer.
眾所周知，他支持愛爾蘭共和軍。

U: B2 [ U ] (an expression of) understanding and care for someone else's suffering
› to express your sadness to someone because a relation or friend of theirs has recently died
› to stop working in order to show your support for other workers who are on strike

example: The president has sent a message of sympathy to the relatives of the dead soldiers.
總統已經向陣亡士兵的家屬發出弔唁電報。
I don't have much sympathy for her - I think she's brought her troubles on herself.
我不太同情她——我覺得她是在自找麻煩。
Compare
empathy
I went along to the funeral in order to offer my sympathies.
我去參加葬禮以表弔慰。
I must confess I have some sympathy with his views.
我必須承認我比較贊同他的觀點。
Of those people questioned, 93 percent said their sympathies were with the teachers.
接受調查的人當中有93%表示支持教師。
He is known to have right-wing sympathies.
大家都知道他支持右派。
The railway workers came out in sympathy with the miners.
鐵路工人加入罷工，聲援煤礦工人。

NONE: › an occasion when a lot of people vote for or support a particular person because he or she has suffered recently
同情票

example: He won the award, but some suspected he got the sympathy vote following his struggle with cancer.
他贏得了這個獎項，但有些人懷疑這是因為他與癌症的抗爭贏得了同情票。

NONE: › a long piece of music for an orchestra, usually with four movements (= parts)
交響樂，交響曲

example: Mahler's ninth symphony
馬勒的《第九交響曲》

NONE: › a place in the body where two bones are directly and permanently joined together by cartilage (= strong tissue)
（骨）聯合縫
› an occasion at which people who have great knowledge of a particular subject meet in order to discuss a matter of interest
研討會，論壇，專題討論會

example: a symposium on European cinema
歐洲電影研討會

NONE: B2 any feeling of illness or physical or mental change that is caused by a particular disease
（疾病的）癥狀
C2 any single problem that is caused by and shows a more serious and general problem
徵兆，徵候

example: He's complaining of all the usual flu symptoms - a high temperature, headache, and so on.
他抱怨所有常見的感冒癥狀——高燒、頭痛等，都出現在他身上。
He's been HIV-positive for six years, but just recently he's started to develop the symptoms of AIDS.
他 HIV 病毒檢測呈陽性反應已有六年了，但直到最近才開始出現愛滋病的徵狀。
It's her feeling that the recent outbreaks of violence are a symptom of the dissatisfaction that is currently affecting our society.
她覺得最近爆發的暴力事件顯示了目前不滿的情緒正在影響我們的社會。

NONE: › If something bad is symptomatic of something else, it is caused by the other thing and is proof that it exists.
表明…存在的，是…的徵兆的
› specialized medical showing symptoms of a particular disease
顯示症狀的

example: Jealousy within a relationship is usually symptomatic of low self-esteem in one of the partners.
嫉妒情緒出現在戀愛關係中時，通常顯示出其中一方欠缺自信。
A doctor who had treated an Ebola patient may have been symptomatic when he boarded the plane.
一位曾治療過伊波拉患者的醫生在登機時可能已顯露症狀。
